1.title: Agents in Foundry
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Agents in Foundry. It covers the exam area Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Create and test a single-agent solution in the Foundry portal. Create a lightweight client application for an agent. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (fifty-five to sixty percent). Exam format: a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes; check the exam page for the time. Validated against: the official A I nine oh one study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: What a Foundry agent is
1.text: What a Foundry agent is. A single agent is "a model paired with instructions and tools that can reason over a request and take action". Foundry Agent Service is "a managed platform for building, deploying and scaling A I agents". Model. The deployed model that reasons. Instructions. The system prompt: the agent's role and behavior. Tools. What the agent can use to find information or act. Kinds of agent.

1.title: What a Foundry agent is, continued
1.text: What a Foundry agent is. Prompt agent. Declaratively defined: you give model, instructions and tools; no hosting code. Voice-based prompt agent. A prompt agent for spoken conversations. Hosted agent. Your own code running in a container, managed by Foundry. Exam tip: The exam's agent is the prompt agent: model plus instructions plus tools. Compare with a plain chat call: the agent adds tools and a managed conversation.

1.title: What a Foundry agent is, continued
1.text: What a Foundry agent is. The figure shows this: A Foundry agent: a model, instructions and tools.

1.title: Tools an agent can use
1.text: Tools an agent can use. File search. Find answers in files you upload. Azure A I Search. Search an index of your content. Web search (and grounding with Bing). Fresh information from the web. Code interpreter. Write and run code, such as calculations or charts. Function calling. Call your own functions; your app runs them (client-side). Open A P I. Call a R E S T (representational state transfer) A P I described by an Open A P I file. M C P (Model Context Protocol). Connect to tools exposed by an M C P server. Agent-to-agent (A to A). Work with another agent.

1.title: Tools an agent can use, continued
1.text: Tools an agent can use. Tools are of two kinds: knowledge tools (find information: file search, web search, A I Search) and action tools (do something: code, functions, A P Is). for the current list, because names change. Exam tip: "Answer from my uploaded documents" to file search. "Do calculations or draw a chart" to code interpreter. "Use today's web information" to web search. "Call my company's own function" to function calling.

1.title: Create and test an agent in the portal
1.text: Create and test an agent in the portal. Open your project in the portal. In Build, choose Agents in the left pane. Select Create agent and give it a name, for example My Agent. Add instructions, for example "You are a helpful writing assistant". Choose the model deployment and add tools if needed. Chat with the agent in the agents playground. Ask a follow-up question to check that the agent keeps the conversation history.

1.title: Create and test an agent in the portal, continued
1.text: Create and test an agent in the portal. The figure shows this: Create an agent: name, instructions, model, tools, then chat to test.

1.title: Call the agent from a client application
1.text: Call the agent from a client application. A lightweight client creates the agent (or uses an existing one), starts a conversation, and sends messages. This is the short program from the Microsoft quickstart. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Call the agent from a client application, continued
1.text: Call the agent from a client application. project dot agents dot create version... Creates the agent, or a new version if it already exists. Prompt Agent Definition model..., instructions... The definition: which model and which instructions. project dot get openai client agent name... A client bound to that agent. openai dot conversations dot create. Starts a conversation that keeps the history. openai dot responses dot create conversation..., input... Sends a message in that conversation. a second responses dot create with the same conversation id. A follow-up question that knows the earlier answers. Exam tip: The conversation id is what gives multi-turn memory to the agent. Without it, each request would be independent. Agent name picks the agent; model is the deployment it uses.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants an assistant that answers questions from a set of uploaded product manuals. Which agent tool fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: File search. File search lets the agent find answers in files you upload.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which three parts define a prompt agent? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Model, instructions, tools. A prompt agent combines a model, instructions and tools.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. In the client program, what makes the agent remember the earlier question in a follow-up? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Using the same conversation id. Messages sent in the same conversation keep the history.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A developer runs create version for an agent name that already exists. What happens? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A new version of that agent is created. The call creates the agent, or a new version if it already exists.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Where do you test an agent without writing code? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The agents playground in the Foundry portal. You can chat with the agent in the portal and ask follow-up questions.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. An agent must run Python calculations and create a chart. Which tool fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Code interpreter. Code interpreter writes and runs code, for example for calculations and charts.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is a single agent? Answer: A model paired with instructions and tools that can reason over a request and take action. Question two. Name the three kinds of Foundry agent. Answer: Prompt agents, voice-based prompt agents and hosted agents. Question three. Which tool runs code? Answer: Code interpreter.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which call creates an agent or a new version? Answer: project.agents.create version. Question five. What keeps the history of a multi-turn chat with an agent? Answer: The conversation. Question six. Which area of the portal holds agents? Answer: Build, then Agents.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Agent: model plus instructions plus tools; Foundry Agent Service manages it. Kinds: prompt (declarative), voice-based prompt, hosted (your code in a container). Tools: file search, A I Search, web search, code interpreter, function calling, Open A P I, M C P, A to A. Portal: Build, Agents, Create agent, name, instructions, model, tools, chat, follow-up. Client: create version(Prompt Agent Definition), get openai client(agent name), conversations.create(), responses.create(conversation equals...). In the next module, we continue the course.
